ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 rider cancellation fee (NS-4); no refund, no account flag; advise the rider via RydeHELP that cancellation fees are voucher-refundable only through NS-7 human review.
ruling.reasoning: The cancellation is attributed to the rider, which routes the case through NS-0 to NS-4 [F4][NS-0]. Under NS-4, an instant booking cancelled within 3 minutes of matching is free; beyond that the $6.61 fee stands [NS-4]. The recorded timeline shows acceptance at 08:40:00 and the rider's own cancellation at 08:46:40, i.e. 6 min 40 s (400 s) after acceptance, well past the 3-minute grace period, and chat #2 confirms the rider decided to cancel because plans changed [F4][F10][NS-4]. The system record (timeline/fare) therefore settles the fee: $6.61 was charged and is the published cancellation amount [F4][F7][NS-4]. Because the fee is validly imposed, the rider's request that it be struck is answered by the NS-4 rule itself, and NS-4 directs no refund and no action — the rider's fairness concern is a matter for discretionary relief, not a fee-waiver condition [F10][NS-4]. Waiting-fee and no-show logic are not in play: this is a rider-initiated cancellation, so NS-1/NS-2 (driver-claimed no-show) and NS-6 (waiting fee) do not apply; the driver's arrival facts (platform arrival at 08:41:25, driver "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 within 40 m and 4 min 25 s within 200 m afterwards) are consistent with the driver being present but are not the basis of the charge [F2][F5][F6][NS-1][NS-6]. Non-metered fixed-fare logic is unaffected by mileage or the driver's approach distance (39 m closest approach), and no ERP/toll or unpublished add-on appears on the record [F1][F7][F8][RD-2][FARE-1]. The driver profile (2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 d) cannot decide anything by itself and, since no refund is due, does not trigger RD-6's account flag [F17][RD-6]. Rider profile facts likewise do not decide the case [F16][RD-6]. No off-route segment exists, so segment_findings is empty [RD-1].
